w: A 3,056m spire in the Verwall Alps nicknamed the 'Matterhorn of Verwall' for its pointed shape (older sources give it as high as 3,059m). Besides the main summit it carries three named satellites: the Pfeilerkopf south top at 2,884m, the Horn at 3,003m, and the lower Kleiner Patteriol at 2,590m.
_facts: 3,056m, called the 'Matterhorn of Verwall' for its shape
older literature records the height as 3,059m
named subsidiary summits: Pfeilerkopf (2,884m), Horn (3,003m), Kleiner Patteriol (2,590m)

w: The eighth-highest peak in the Lechtal Alps at 2,889m, first climbed in 1855 by locals from the village of Kaisers in the Lech valley. The Lech Valley Ridgeway crosses its southeastern flank on the stretch between the Kaiserjochhaus and the Ansbacher Hut, part of one of Tyrol's classic long-distance hiking routes.
s: First climbed in 1855 by Lech valley locals
_facts: 2,889m, eighth-highest peak in the Lechtal Alps
first ascent recorded in 1855 by locals from Kaisers
crossed by the Lech Valley Ridgeway between Kaiserjochhaus and Ansbacher Hut

w: The pass that gives Vorarlberg its name - 'before the Arl mountain' - carrying the border between Tyrol and Vorarlberg. Its ring of resorts, Lech, Zurs, Stuben, St. Christoph, St. Anton, Oberlech, Stubenbach, Zug and Warth, makes it one of the Alps' densest clusters of ski villages under one pass name.
_facts: mountain pass carrying the Tyrol-Vorarlberg border
gives the state of Vorarlberg its name ('before the Arl')
resorts on the pass include Lech, Zurs, Stuben, St. Christoph, St. Anton, Oberlech, Stubenbach, Zug and Warth

w: A 1,773m pass linking the upper Lech valley - Warth, Lech, Zurs - to the Klostertal near Stuben, built in stages from 1897 after the 1884 Arlberg railway made a road necessity. A tunnel and a bridge over the Hölltobel followed; Marshall Plan funds paid for further safety work from 1948.
_facts: 1,773m pass linking the Lech valley to the Klostertal near Stuben
first road stretch opened in October 1897, spurred by the 1884 Arlberg railway
widened into the Lech valley by 1909; open in winter since 1936
Marshall Plan funds improved avalanche safety from 1948
